body:
### Summary

# Summary

On aarch64 Linux, uv 0.11.8 occasionally dies with SIGABRT (exit 134), silently, during any cold-cache operation that downloads from the index (uv run/uv sync/uv pip install).

Warm cache never triggers it.

Output is just the usual progress lines, then a core dump — no error.

# Backtrace (rebuilt with debug info; shipped binaries are stripped):
```
abort() ← AWS-LC rand_bytes_core (rand.c) ← RAND_bytes ← aws_lc_rs::rand::fill
        ← rustls SessionId::random ← rustls ClientConnection::new ← tokio-rustls/reqwest connect
```

# Root cause

uv downloads over HTTPS.  rustls (default provider aws-lc-rs) calls RAND_bytes per handshake.

On aarch64 FEAT_RNG CPUs, AWS-LC uses the RNDR instruction with no retry (rndr-armv8.pl); a single transient RNDR failure aborts the process.

# Upstream

aws/aws-lc#3453 (also aws/aws-lc-rs).

# Environment

GCP Axion (n4a, Neoverse-N3), aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04; ~3–4% of downloads, clustered on some physical hosts; both the musl-static and glibc uv builds affected; also expected
on Graviton3/4.

# Workaround (no rebuild)

OPENSSL_armcap=~0x20000 in uv's environment → AWS-LC skips RNDR → 0 aborts across 380 builds (vs ~4–5%), AES/SHA acceleration retained.

# Ask

It's ultimately an AWS-LC bug, but uv is where it surfaces as a hard crash for arm64 cloud users. Could uv document the workaround, track the AWS-LC fix, and/or consider preferring
OS getrandom over RNDR on aarch64 (or a config knob)?

### Platform

Ubuntu 24.04 on GCP, n4a

### Version

0.11.8

### Python version

3.14.4
title: Intermittent SIGABRT on aarch64 (GCP Axion / AWS Graviton) during package downloads - AWS-LC RNDR no-retry
